tracks.title: Panel B, Panel B, Panel B
tracks.subject: a man in a Swindon back garden assembling a flat-pack shed on a Saturday and finding the kit has three wall panels stamped B and none stamped C, so he builds it anyway with the window facing the fence
tracks.caption: Skiffle revival, 1950s British skiffle party style. Fast strummed acoustic guitar on boom-chick rhythm, scratched washboard with thimbles, thumping tea-chest bass, wailing harmonica fills between lines. Dry live front-room recording, close mics, small room. Male tenor, clearly sung melody, bright music-hall phrasing with group shouts on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 168 BPM, G major. Cheerful, flustered, grinning. No electric guitars, no drum kit, no synths, no autotune, no modern pop production.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - washboard, strummed guitar]

[Verse 1]
Saturday morning, the van's been and gone
Forty-two pieces and one little spanner
I laid them all out on the lawn in a row
And the instructions are written in Swedish

[Pre-Chorus]
I looked for C and I looked again
All I found was B, B, B

[Chorus]
Panel B, panel B, panel B
Where's the panel that they owe to me
I'll screw it together, I'll make it agree
With panel B, panel B, panel B

[Verse 2]
The roof's on now and it's leaning a bit
The door opens inward and hits the mower
The window's lovely, a proper bay
And it looks straight out at the fence

[Pre-Chorus]
My wife came out with a mug of tea
She said love, is that meant to be

[Chorus]
Panel B, panel B, panel B
Nobody's sending a panel C
I'm calling it finished, it's standing for me
On panel B, panel B, panel B

[Outro - harmonica, last washboard roll]
Three panel B's and a view of the fence

tracks.title: The Knee That Clicks
tracks.subject: a wife who says she can find her husband in a dark house by the click of his left knee on every step, and he takes her out dancing on their anniversary so she can hear it keep time
tracks.caption: Big band swing, 1950s Sinatra-era style. Muted trumpet section stabs, warm saxophone section pads and unison lines, walking upright bass, swung brushed drums with ride cymbal, stride piano fills. Lush live big band recording with natural room reverb. Male baritone, clearly sung melody, full open tone, relaxed swing phrasing. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 132 BPM, B-flat major. Warm, affectionate, smiling. No synths, no electric guitar, no autotune, no hip-hop beats, no modern pop drums.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - sax section, walking bass]

[Verse 1]
My left knee clicks on every stair
It's done it since I was forty
The doctor says it's only air
And tells me not to worry

[Pre-Chorus]
But you say in the dark you know it's me
Before I reach the landing

[Chorus]
Click, click, there goes my knee
You say it's how you find me
You don't need the hallway light
You just listen for the clicking

[Verse 2]
So Saturday I booked a band
And a table by the floor
I took you gently by the hand
Like thirty years before

[Pre-Chorus]
And over all the trumpets playing
You heard my knee keep time

[Chorus]
Click, click, there goes my knee
And you're laughing on my shoulder
Every step is one more year
And it clicks a little louder

[Outro - brass swell, brushed drums]
Click, click, darling, dance with me

tracks.title: Same Heel Again
tracks.subject: a woman who runs a one-person shoe repair kiosk in Lewisham and realises the man who brings in the same brown brogue with a worn heel every second week has been walking it down on purpose
tracks.caption: UK lovers rock, late-1970s London reggae ballad style. One-drop reggae drums with soft rimshots, deep round bass guitar, offbeat skank guitar, warm Rhodes electric piano chords. Warm analogue studio sound with light spring reverb. Female soprano, clearly sung melody, smooth and sweet with soft harmony vocals. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 76 BPM, F major. Tender, shy, romantic. No dancehall, no trap drums, no autotune, no rap, no EDM synths.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes, bass line]

[Verse 1]
Little kiosk by the station
Glue and polish, one small stool
Every second Monday morning
You come in with the same left shoe

[Pre-Chorus]
Brown brogue, the heel worn thin
You smile and say it's how you walk

[Chorus]
Same heel again, same heel again
Nobody wears a shoe that fast
Same heel again, I fix it then
I hope you wear it out at last

[Verse 2]
I keep your ticket by the till
I know your number off by heart
You stand and talk while the glue dries
And never look at what I charge

[Pre-Chorus]
Today you brought the right shoe too
And asked me what I do at six

[Chorus]
Same heel again, same heel again
So that's why you scuff it so
Same heel again, it's six, and then
I'll lock the shutter and we'll go

[Outro - skank guitar, Rhodes]
Same heel again, walk me home

tracks.title: Day Three of the Hiccups
tracks.subject: a man in Croydon who has had the hiccups for three days, working through every cure his coworkers swear by, sugar, a paper bag, drinking upside down, a sudden shout from behind, and none of them working
tracks.caption: Synthwave, retro 1980s outrun style. Pulsing analogue bass arpeggio, gated reverb drums with big snare, bright polysynth lead melody, clean electric guitar lead line in the solo. Glossy 80s production, wide stereo chorus, neon night atmosphere. Male tenor, clearly sung melody, strong 80s pop delivery. tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - bass arpeggio, gated drums]

[Verse 1]
Monday at the meeting, I said hic
Tuesday on the train, I said hic
Every forty seconds, on the dot
Half a sentence is all I've got

[Pre-Chorus]
Janet says a spoon of sugar
Dev says hold your breath

[Chorus]
Day three of the hiccups
And the city's lit up blue

tracks.title: แมวส้มข้ามระเบียง
tracks.genre: Thai mahori-ensemble classical song (phleng Thai doem)
tracks.subject: a man whose neighbour's orange cat crosses onto his balcony every night, so each night he carries it back to her door, until the night the cat does not come and she knocks on his door herself
tracks.caption: Thai mahori-ensemble classical song in phleng Thai doem form with modern words. High nasal saw duang leading, mellow saw u answering, plucked jakhe drone notes, hammered khim tremolo, small ching cymbals keeping the cycle. Intimate acoustic recording in a natural wooden room. Male lead with warm mid-register classical Thai voice and gentle melisma at line ends, clearly sung. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 72 BPM, C major pentatonic. Courtly, hopeful love song. No drum kit, no synths, no Western strings, no pop chords, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - saw duang melody over khim, ching keeping time]
[Verse 1]
แมวส้มของเธอข้ามระเบียง
มานอนเคียงรองเท้าฉันทุกคืน
ฉันอุ้มมันไปคืนที่ประตู
เธอยิ้มรับแล้วยื่นขนมให้
[Pre-Chorus]
พรุ่งนี้มันมาอีกนะ
ฉันแอบหวังให้มันมา
[Chorus]
แมวเอ๋ยแมวส้ม
ช่วยพาฉันไปเคาะประตู
อีกสักคืนให้ฉันได้รู้
ว่าเธอรอฉันหรือรอแมว
[Verse 2]
คืนนี้แมวไม่มาเลย
ฉันนั่งเฉยกับปลาทูหนึ่งตัว
แล้วเสียงเคาะดังที่ประตู
เธอยืนอยู่ ไม่มีแมว
[Chorus]
แมวเอ๋ยแมวส้ม
วันนี้ไม่ต้องพาใครมา
เธอบอกแมวหลับไปแล้วล่ะ
แต่เธออยากเดินมาเอง
[Outro - khim tremolo, saw u closing phrase, ching]
ปลาทูตัวนั้น แบ่งกันคนละครึ่ง
